_about: Every board, kit, module and part the project uses, one entry each. Source for docs/parts-catalog.md (tools/render_parts.py). Add an entry when a part is bought, and add the demo to used_in when a demo uses it. Prices are what was paid or read on the date given; check before quoting. A buy entry's url is the seller's page, opened and read on that entry's date; no url means none was checked.
categories: Plug-on boards (BoosterPack plug-in modules) and debuggers

parts.name: LP-MSPM0G3507 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's 80 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ board with 128 kB flash and 32 kB RAM, a built-in debugger, three buttons, two LEDs (one RGB) and light and temperature sensors.
use_for: Most demos here start here: plenty of RAM for displays and AI models
Touchscreen projects (with the Waveshare display)
Motor control and CAN bus
parts.connect: One USB cable powers, programs and debugs it. 40-pin BoosterPack header, 3.3 V logic.

buy.note: price shown without a login on 2026-10-09; stock and ordering need a myTI login (in stock on the 2026-10-08 logged-in read)
0 in stock that day

parts.name: LP-MSPM0L1306 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's low-cost 32 MHz Cortex-M0+ board with 64 kB flash and only 4 kB RAM, a built-in debugger, LEDs, buttons, a light sensor and a thermistor.
use_for: Showing what fits in a 65-cent chip (1,000-unit price)
Simple sensor and LED projects
Edge AI models (handwritten digits, room occupancy)
parts.connect: One USB cable. 40-pin header, 3.3 V logic. J16 and J17 choose whether the serial pins go to USB or to the header.

buy.note: in stock that day

parts.name: LP-MSPM0L2228 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's 32 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ board with 256 kB flash and 32 kB RAM, a built-in debugger with EnergyTrace, a 7-segment LCD on the board, an RGB LED, a red LED, two buttons, two crystals and a 100 mF super capacitor on a battery-backed island.
use_for: Segment LCD projects: the chip drives the glass itself
Battery and super-capacitor projects: real-time clock and tamper pins that live on when the main supply is gone
Low-power sensor nodes with a readout on the board
parts.connect: One USB cable powers, programs and debugs it. 40-pin BoosterPack header, 3.3 V logic. J17 and J18 send the chip's UART0 to the USB serial port.

buy.note: the tool page showed no price and 'Out of stock on TI.com' without a login on 2026-11-09

parts.name: LP-MSPM0C1104 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's smallest MSPM0 board: a 24 MHz Cortex-M0+ chip with 16 kB flash and 1 kB RAM, a built-in debugger, one red LED and one button, on a 20-pin header with female sockets.
use_for: The cheapest blink-to-sensor demos
Finding out which demos fit in 1 kB of RAM
Comparing with 10-cent chips from other makers
parts.connect: One micro-USB cable, not in the box. 20-pin header with female sockets (use male-ended jumpers), 3.3 V logic, 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups already fitted on PA11 and PA0. J101's RXD and TXD shunts send the serial pins to USB or only to the header. The LED moved from PA4 (board version E2) to PA22 (E3).
parts.status: in hand (one of two; the second is sealed)
parts._merge_note: update of the existing entry: connect text, used_in, learn, faq. Price confirmed from the order; TI.com page showed no price to a logged-out fetch on 2026-10-07 (inventory 3,464). data/boards.csv still says 5.99

parts.name: LP-EM-CC2340R5 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's Bluetooth Low Energy and Zigbee board (CC2340R52 chip). Needs a separate XDS110 debugger to program it.
use_for: Bluetooth sensors and beacons
Zigbee devices for Home Assistant
Thread radio for a border router
parts.connect: Programs through an LP-XDS110ET or another LaunchPad kit's debugger. 40-pin header, 3.3 V.

parts.name: LP-CC1354P10-1 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's sub-1 GHz plus 2.4 GHz radio board: Zigbee, Thread, Bluetooth and long-range sub-1 GHz.
use_for: Zigbee coordinator
Thread border-router host (the LP-EM-CC2340R5 is its radio)
Long-range sub-1 GHz links
parts.connect: One USB cable, built-in debugger. 40-pin header, 3.3 V.

parts.name: LAUNCHXL-F2800137 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's C2000 real-time control board: a 120 MHz chip built for motor control and power conversion, with a math unit for sine and cosine.
use_for: Motor control demos
Fast control loops
Comparing control speed with other chips
parts.connect: One USB cable, built-in debugger. Two BoosterPack sites; site 1 has no I2C on pins 9 and 10.

buy.note: in stock that day

parts.name: LP-XDS110ET debugger
parts.what: TI's stand-alone debug probe with EnergyTrace: powers, programs and measures the current of boards that have no built-in debugger, such as the LP-EM radio boards.
use_for: Programming LP-EM-CC2340R5, CC2755 and CC35xx boards
Measuring a board's current with EnergyTrace (700 nA to 400 mA per TI's quick start guide)
A serial port to the Mac for the board's text output
parts.connect: USB-C to the Mac (cable in the box). The LP-EM board's 20-pin edge goes into the probe's 20-pin socket. TGT VDD jumper on XDS when the probe powers the board (CC2340R5, CC2755P10, and needed for EnergyTrace); on EXT when the board powers itself (CC35X1). One LP-EM board at a time.

buy.note: in stock that day (out of stock on 2026-10-07); TI.com order T07011659

parts.name: BOOSTXL-EDUMKII Educational BoosterPack MKII
parts.what: A plug-on board full of inputs and outputs: a 128 x 128 color screen, joystick, two buttons, buzzer, color LED, microphone, accelerometer, light sensor and a servo header.
use_for: Games and menus on the color screen
Joystick and button demos
Sound and light demos
parts.connect: Needs 3.3 V and 5 V. Plugs straight onto the LP-MSPM0G3507 (pull J8, J9, J16 to J18; J21 and J22 down) and nearly onto the G3519, CC1354P10, MSPM33C321A and AM13E230. The L1306, CC2340R5 and F2800137 lose parts and need a wire for the screen (pin 31). Does not fit the C1104. Jumper J5 on the board: 2-3 for the screen backlight.
parts.status: in hand, stacked on the LP-MSPM33C321A

parts.name: BP-BASSENSORSMKII Sensors BoosterPack plug-in module
parts.what: A plug-on board of TI and Bosch sensors on one I2C bus. The TMP117 reads temperature and sits on a break-away board with a ribbon cable. The HDC2080 reads temperature and humidity, the OPT3001 light, the BMI160 motion, with a BMM150 compass behind it, and the DRV5055 a magnet. Red and green LEDs.
use_for: Weather and room-comfort demos
Motion and tilt demos
The same sensor demo on every MSPM0 board
parts.connect: Plugs on (I2C on pins 9, 10; pull-ups on the board). Plug the ribbon cable into J5 and J6 or the TMP117 reads nothing. All six sensors on the G3507 (five jumpers out), G3519 and CC1354P10; the L1306 needs two wires to power the OPT3001 and TMP117; the C1104 reads two of six; the CC2755P10 needs TI's three wires; the F2800137 has no I2C on these pins.
parts.status: in hand, stacked on the LP-MSPM0G5187: humidity and temperature, light and the magnet sensor read live; the BMI160 did not answer and the TMP117 needs its ribbon cable (see its guide)

parts.name: BOOSTXL-SHARP128 display BoosterPack plug-in module
parts.what: A plug-on 128 x 128 black-and-white Sharp memory display with a microSD slot. It draws almost no power and keeps its image.
use_for: The one display that plugs onto most boards here
Clocks, sensor readouts, battery-powered screens
parts.connect: Uses pins 2, 5, 6, 7, 15 for the screen (8, 14, 17 for the SD card). Plugs on with no wires on the G3507, L1306, G3519, C1104, CC1354P10, MSPM33C321A and AM13E230; one wire on the F2800137 (6 to 13). The CC2340R5 and CC2755P10 need resistor work for the screen and one wire for the SD card. 3.3 V only. Pin 19 is not used as shipped.

parts.name: BOOSTXL-AUDIO audio BoosterPack plug-in module
parts.what: A plug-on speaker board: a DAC8311 16-bit DAC and a TPA301 amplifier driving a small speaker, plus an electret microphone with a preamp.
use_for: Sound out from a board with no audio of its own
Chiptune, tones and voice prompts
Microphone input for level meters and wake words
parts.connect: DAC8311 on SPI (pins 7, 15, 12), microphone on pin 6. Jumper J5 picks what drives the amplifier: the SPI DAC (default), the board's own DAC on pin 30, or PWM on pin 19. Plugs on with no clash on the MSPM33C321A and AM13E230; pin 6 clashes on the G3507, pins 13 and 30 on the L1306. Pins 12 and 13 are low confidence until measured.

parts.name: BP-CC1407P-9-FE sub-1 GHz radio BoosterPack plug-in module
parts.what: A sub-1 GHz radio (CC1407P, 902 to 928 MHz on this board) on a plug-on board, with no processor of its own: a LaunchPad kit drives it over SPI. Up to +22 dBm, SMA antenna socket, red and green LEDs.
use_for: Long-range radio links where 2.4 GHz does not reach
A radio for a host chip that has none (MSPM0, MSPM33)
Range tests at 915 MHz
parts.connect: Plugs onto a LaunchPad kit (pins 1, 7, 14, 15, 18, 23, 36). TI supports the LP-CC1354P10-1 and four other CC13xx/CC26xx boards with its TRX plug-in, and the CC2745R10 with a Zephyr shield. On the LP-EM-CC2755P10: one wire (23 to 10) and its red LED jumper off. Needs a 915 MHz SMA antenna, not in the kit.

parts.name: Freenove Ultimate Starter Kit for Raspberry Pi Pico, board not included (FNK0058)
parts.what: A box of the classic hobby parts with a breadboard and wires. Made for the Pico, and most parts work at 3.3 V. The HC-SR04 and the L293D need 5 V; the LED module and LCD1602 were not checked.
use_for: IR remote control
7-segment counters and an 8 x 8 LED matrix
Keypad lock, servo, DC motor and stepper
DHT11 temperature and humidity, the most popular hobby demo
RFID, PIR motion, ultrasonic distance, LCD1602 screen
parts.contents: I2C LCD1602, IR remote and receiver, 4-digit and 1-digit 7-segment displays with two 74HC595, 8 x 8 LED matrix, 8-LED WS2812-type module, 4 x 4 keypad, active and passive buzzers, L293D, DC motor, servo, stepper with driver board, DHT11, thermistor, photoresistor, joystick, PIR, HC-SR04, MPU6050, RFID, relay, breadboard power module, breadboard, jumper wires (Freenove's parts list).
parts.connect: Breadboard and jumper wires. Motors and the LED module run from the breadboard power module or the LaunchPad kit's 5 V pin, grounds tied together. The HC-SR04 is a 5 V part: use the RCWL-1601 instead.
parts.status: arrived 2026-10-09 (box reads 'Freenove Ultimate Starter Kit without Pico', FNK0058 B)

parts.name: Waveshare 3.5 inch capacitive touch LCD (ST7796S screen, FT6336U touch)
parts.what: A 320 x 480 color screen with a finger-touch panel, wired to the board by hand.
use_for: Touchscreen demos: draw a digit and the board reads it
Photo and graphics demos
LVGL user interfaces
parts.connect: 12 jumper wires (13 with MISO) to the LP-MSPM0G3507 (SPI for the screen, software I2C for touch on PB3 and PB2). Chip select needs 10 microseconds high between commands.

parts.name: Freenove 8-LED RGB ring module, WS2812 type (from the Freenove kit)
parts.what: Eight color LEDs in a ring on one data wire, labelled D1 to D8 on the board. Each LED is set to any color from software.
use_for: Color status light
Spinner and progress ring
Testing a WS2812 driver on a chip with no library for it
parts.connect: 3 pins: 5 V power, GND, data in. Read the pin names on the board before wiring. Whether its data pin accepts 3.3 V logic on a 5 V supply is unknown.

buy.note: in the kit; no separate price

parts.name: ELEGOO 0.96 inch OLED, 128 x 64, SSD1306, 3 pack
parts.what: The most-used small hobby screen: sharp white-on-black text and graphics.
use_for: Sensor readouts
Tiny games
Status screens on any board
parts.connect: 4 wires, pins as printed on the board in this order: GND, VCC, SCL, SDA. Power it from 3.3 V (I2C address 0x3C). The order differs between makers, so wire by the printed names.

parts.name: DIYables TM1637 4-digit 7-segment display with colon, 2 pack
parts.what: Four big LED digits with a colon, driven over two wires.
use_for: Clocks
Timers and countdowns
Counters and scoreboards
parts.connect: 4 wires: power, GND, CLK, DIO (2-wire protocol of its own, not I2C). The pin names are not readable in the photo; read them on the board before wiring. Power it from 3.3 V: the TM1637 datasheet only tests 4.5 to 5.5 V, but Seeed rates its TM1637 module for 3.3 to 5.5 V.

parts.name: PIR motion sensor module, HC-SR501 type (from the Freenove kit)
parts.what: Sees warm bodies move in front of it with a clear dome lens. Two trim pots set how far it sees and how long its output stays high. Made for 5 V power; its output pin is 3.3 V.
use_for: Motion-triggered light or alarm
Presence detection to compare against the mmWave radar
Wake-on-motion for a battery project
parts.connect: 3 pins: power, OUT, GND. The pin names are not readable in the photo; read them on the board before wiring. Power from 5 V (the LaunchPad kit's 5 V pin or the breadboard power module); the output pin swings to 3.3 V, safe for the LaunchPad. Give it about a minute to settle after power-up.

buy.note: in the kit; no separate price

parts.name: Adafruit VL53L1X laser distance sensor, STEMMA QT (Adafruit 3967)
parts.what: Measures distance with an invisible laser, about 3 cm to 4 m.
use_for: Presence and proximity
Gesture and hand-wave demos
A laser ruler
parts.connect: Qwiic cable (I2C, address 0x29). Works from 3.3 V.

buy.note: page not readable 2026-11-09

parts.name: Adafruit RCWL-1601 ultrasonic distance sensor (Adafruit 4007)
parts.what: Bounces sound off things to measure distance; a 3.3 V-safe version of the classic HC-SR04.
use_for: Parking sensor
Robot obstacle detection
The HC-SR04 projects, on a 3.3 V board
parts.connect: 4 pins, as printed left to right (photo, front): VCC, Trig/Rx, Echo/Tx, Gnd. The board also prints SCL and SDA beside Trig/Rx and Echo/Tx for its I2C and serial modes; for the HC-SR04 style use Trig and Echo. Works at 3 V or 5 V.

buy.note: DigiKey number 1528-2832-ND matches Adafruit 2832 (a NeoPixel RGBW strip), not Adafruit 4007; page not read, number unverified 2026-11-09

parts.status: arrived 2026-10-09 (board reads RCWL-1601 with a 4-pin header fitted)

parts.name: HiLetgo DRV8833 dual motor driver, 3 pack (TI DRV8833 chip)
parts.what: Lets a LaunchPad kit's pin run a DC motor forward, backward and at any speed.
use_for: Spinning the kit's DC motor
Small robots and fans
parts.connect: Two pins per motor from the LaunchPad kit (3.3 V logic). Motor power from the breadboard power module, grounds tied together. Two rows of 8 holes with no header fitted; the pin names are on the back of the board, which is not in the photo: read them before wiring.

parts.name: Taiss KY-040 rotary encoder with push button, 5 pack
parts.what: A clicky knob that turns forever: the board counts clicks and direction, and the knob also pushes like a button.
use_for: Menus and volume knobs
Setting a timer or a motor speed
The G3507's hardware knob-counting input (QEI)
parts.connect: 5 pins, as printed top to bottom: GND, + (power), SW (push switch), DT, CLK. Power it from 3.3 V. The knob presses onto the shaft.

parts.name: Adafruit STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable to female sockets, 150 mm (Adafruit 4397)
parts.what: Plugs any Qwiic sensor onto a LaunchPad kit's header pins with no soldering.
use_for: Adding Qwiic sensors to any board here
parts.connect: Black GND, red 3.3 V, blue SDA, yellow SCL, onto the LaunchPad kit's I2C header pins.

parts.name: Adafruit STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable to male pins, 150 mm (Adafruit 4209)
parts.what: The same cable with pins instead of sockets, for the C1104's socket header or a breadboard.
use_for: Qwiic sensors on the LP-MSPM0C1104
Qwiic sensors on a breadboard
parts.connect: Same colors as above.

parts.name: ELEGOO jumper wires (120-piece pack)
parts.what: Male and female breadboard wires for connecting anything to anything.
use_for: Wiring displays and modules
Loop tests that wire a board's pins to each other
parts.connect: Push onto header pins or into a breadboard.

parts.name: ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1-N8 (Espressif)
parts.what: Espressif's entry board for the ESP32-C6: one 160 MHz RISC-V core, 512 kB RAM, 8 MB flash in the module, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth LE 5, Zigbee and Thread on one antenna. Two USB-C ports, no separate debugger needed.
use_for: ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, so Home Assistant in Docker hears BTHome sensors
The comparison board for the LP-EM-CC2340R5 and LP-EM-CC2755P10: the same tests side by side
Zigbee and Thread devices for Home Assistant with Espressif's SDKs
The yardstick for ESPHome on TI chips
parts.connect: One USB-C data cable (not in the bag) into the port marked USB: flashing, serial log and debugging in one. The port marked UART is a USB-to-UART chip on GPIO16 and GPIO17. 32 header pins, 3.3 V logic. J5 is the current-measurement jumper.

buy.note: two bought; price from the staged cart, order page not read back

parts.status: one in hand (the Bluetooth proxy board), one sealed

parts.name: LP-MSPM0G3519 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's 80 MHz Cortex-M0+ board with 512 kB flash and 128 kB RAM, two fast ADCs, a DAC, a math accelerator, AES, true random numbers, two CAN-FD ports and a debugger that measures current (EnergyTrace).
use_for: The main MSPM0 board: everything that ran on the LP-MSPM0G3507, with four times the memory
Zephyr (upstream board lp_mspm0g3519)
Hosting BoosterPacks: sensors, displays, the CC1407P sub-1 GHz radio
Post-quantum crypto examples (ML-KEM, ML-DSA)
parts.connect: One USB cable (USB-A to micro-B, in the box). 80-pin BoosterPack header (two sites), 3.3 V logic. J12 and J13 switch PA10 and PA11 between the USB serial port and the header. 4.7 kΩ I2C pull-ups on PC2 and PC3 (J14, J15).

parts.name: SK-TDA4VM starter kit (TDA4VM Jacinto 7 vision processor, J721EXSKG01EVM)
parts.what: TI's Linux vision board: two Cortex-A72 cores, a C7x DSP with an 8 TOPS matrix accelerator for neural networks, a GPU, an image signal processor and hardware H.264 and H.265 video decode (H.264 encode), with 4 GB of memory. Comes with a micro-SD card and a serial cable. No power supply, camera or Wi-Fi card in the box. Kit name still to confirm from a photo.
use_for: Neural-network speed on a real accelerator, against TI's published numbers and against the CPU
Video decode and encode speed, and GStreamer camera pipelines
The CPU, memory and boot-time tests on a Linux board
Rebuilding NVIDIA Holoscan demos' operator graphs on TI parts
parts.connect: Power through the USB-C port J14 from a 20 V supply (5 V can reset it). Serial console on the micro-B port J4 (four ports, the Linux console is the third, 115200). Ethernet for SSH. Boot from the micro-SD card with switch SW1 all OFF. USB webcam on any USB-A port; the CSI ports take a Raspberry Pi Camera Module v2 (IMX219).

buy.price: not shown to a logged-out reader

parts.status: no longer on the bench (2026-10-31); results kept

parts.name: BeagleY-AI (TI AM67A vision processor)
parts.what: A credit-card Linux board on TI's AM67A: four Arm Cortex-A53 cores at 1.4 GHz, a GPU, a 4 TOPS neural accelerator, H.264 and H.265 video, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, HDMI out and a Raspberry Pi style 40-pin header.
use_for: Camera demos: object detection and body pose (replaces the SK-TDA4VM)
Motion games for kids on a TV
An emulator box at the TV
parts.connect: USB-C power, microSD card for the system, HDMI out, USB for cameras and controllers, 40-pin header at 3.3 V.

buy.note: price on the 2026-10-07 check; the order's own seller and price not recorded

parts.status: in hand, arrived 2026-11-03; on the bench

parts.name: USB-C power supply that gives 20 V at 3 A or more (60 W class), for the SK-TDA4VM
parts.what: A USB Power Delivery wall charger that can negotiate 20 V. TI's user guide lists two tested models: GlobTek TR9CZ3000USBCG2R6BF2 and Qualtek QADC-65-20-08CB (65 W). A 5 V charger can reset the board during boot.
use_for: Powering the SK-TDA4VM
parts.connect: Charger to the board's USB-C power port J14 (its status LED is LD3). Do not use the USB-C data port J12 for power.
parts.status: to order only if you have no 20 V USB-C charger

parts.name: LP-MSPM0G5187 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's 80 MHz Cortex-M0+ board with a TinyEngine neural accelerator, 128 kB flash and 32 kB RAM. The chip has USB and I2S audio. The board adds a microphone, an audio ADC, a microSD slot and a debugger that measures current.
use_for: Neural nets in hardware: CPU against NPU on the same model
Wake-word and gesture demos
USB microphone and first sound through an I2S DAC
parts.connect: One USB-C cable for the debugger (USB-A to USB-C in the box); a second USB-C port for the chip's own USB. 40-pin header, 3.3 V logic. I2S on header pins 27 to 30. J6 powers the microphone, audio ADC and SD slot.

parts.name: LP-MSPM33C321A LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's 160 MHz Cortex-M33 board with 1 MB flash and 256 kB RAM, TrustZone and security hardware, a built-in 128 x 32 OLED screen, 8 MB of QSPI flash and a debug probe that measures current (EnergyTrace). A prototype kit sold in limited quantity.
use_for: Touchscreen interfaces with LVGL (TI ships a demo for the Waveshare 3.5 inch display used here)
Post-quantum and classic encryption speed tests
Comparing a Cortex-M33 with the MSPM0's Cortex-M0+ at the same clock
Status screens on the onboard OLED with no wiring
parts.connect: One USB cable (in the box). 80-pin BoosterPack headers plus a mikroBUS socket, 3.3 V logic. J101 joins the debug probe to the chip: lift TXD>> when TI's display demo uses PA10. The OLED and QSPI flash are on the board; the flash holds the out-of-box video.

parts.name: LP-AM13E230 LaunchPad development kit
parts.what: TI's Arm motor-control board: a 200 MHz Cortex-M33 with a trig math unit and a neural-network accelerator (NPU), five motor PWM modules, three fast ADCs, an isolated debug probe and a CAN-FD transceiver. Prototype silicon and a short-term SDK; sold in limited quantity.
use_for: Control-loop speed against the C2000 F2800137 with the same code
AI models on an NPU against the CPU
Motor projects with a motor BoosterPack (not bought) or a small DRV8833 board
Porting STM32G4 code (TI ships a compatibility layer)
parts.connect: One USB-C cable (in the box). 40-pin BoosterPack headers, 3.3 V logic; motor BoosterPacks such as BOOSTXL-DRV8323RS plug straight on. J10 is the chip's power-measurement header. Revision E1 boards (MCU178E1 on the back) use different pins.

parts.name: LP-AM243 LaunchPad development kit (AM243x Sitara MCU)
parts.what: TI's Arm real-time board with four Cortex-R5F cores at 800 MHz, a Cortex-M4F, two gigabit PRU-ICSSG industrial-Ethernet engines, 2 MB of on-chip RAM, 64 MB of quad SPI flash and two gigabit Ethernet ports.
use_for: Control-loop speed with the same code as the AM263P at twice the clock
Gigabit and industrial-Ethernet projects
Custom fast peripherals on PRU cores
parts.connect: Two cables. A USB Type-C charger of 5 V at 3 A powers the board (not in the box, and it must advertise 3 A: a laptop charger worked, a USB-A adapter cable will not). A micro-B cable to J20 is the debugger and serial port (not in the box). Programs load to RAM with SW4 as shipped. Never run TI's security key writer: it is a one-way change.

buy.note: In stock when read; price not shown

parts.name: LP-AM263P LaunchPad development kit (AM263Px Sitara MCU; kit to confirm by photo)
parts.what: TI's Arm real-time board: a chip with four Cortex-R5F cores at 400 MHz, a trig math unit on each core, five 4 Msps ADCs, 20 comparators, 32 PWM modules, 3 MB of on-chip RAM and a 32 MB octal flash, plus two gigabit Ethernet ports, CAN-FD and an industrial-Ethernet engine. The cores can run in lockstep for safety.
use_for: Control-loop speed against the C2000 F2800137 and the AM13E230 with the same code
Running two or four control loops on separate cores
Flash execute-in-place with a cache, against code in RAM
Gigabit Ethernet and industrial-Ethernet projects
parts.connect: Two cables. A USB Type-C supply of 5 V at 3 A powers the board (not in the box). The USB micro-B cable in the box is the debugger and serial port. The box also holds a micro SD card and a CAT5 cable. Two BoosterPack sites, 3.3 V logic. Boot mode is set by the DIP switch SW1. Never run TI's security key writer: it is a one-way change.

buy.note: price not listed; shown out of stock on 2026-10-09; the plan treats the kit name as a variable until a photo confirms it (the TMDSCNCD263P controlCARD uses the same SDK)

parts.name: NXP FRDM-MCXA153 development board
parts.what: NXP's low-cost 96 MHz Cortex-M33 board with 128 kB flash and 32 kB RAM (the same memory as the LP-MSPM0G3507), a built-in MCU-Link debugger, an RGB LED, a temperature sensor and Arduino headers. The core has no floating-point unit.
use_for: Comparing a Cortex-M33 with a Cortex-M0+ at the same memory
Motor-control style loops (motor PWM and encoder input on the chip)
Arduino-shield and mikroBUS click-board projects
parts.connect: USB-C into J15 (MCU-LINK, the top port) for flashing and serial; J8 is the chip's own USB. Arduino Uno sockets, 3.3 V logic. Keep jumper JP2 fitted: it carries the chip's power.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 H (SC1632)
parts.what: Raspberry Pi's board with headers fitted: the RP2350 chip with two Arm Cortex-M33 or two RISC-V cores at 150 MHz, 520 kB RAM and 4 MB flash. No debugger on the board: programs go on by drag and drop.
use_for: The hobbyist baseline every TI board is compared with
The Freenove kit's projects, which were written for this board
Bigger models and demos: every one in this project fits its RAM
parts.connect: Micro-USB (cable not included; USB-C to micro-B for this Mac). Hold BOOTSEL while plugging in to load a program. 40 pins on a breadboard, 3.3 V logic; VBUS gives 5 V from USB.

parts.name: NUCLEO-G071RB (ST Nucleo-64 board)
parts.what: ST's 64 MHz Cortex-M0+ board with 128 kB flash and 36 kB RAM, a built-in ST-LINK debugger on USB Micro-B, a green LED, a button and ARDUINO Uno sockets. No AES or random-number hardware.

parts.name: DRV8376EVM three-phase motor driver evaluation module
parts.what: TI's evaluation board for the DRV8376, a three-phase brushless motor driver with the six power transistors inside one chip (4.5 to 65 V, 4.5 A peak), current sensing built in, and 3.3 V and 5 V regulators on the chip. The board is a 40-pin BoosterPack: it plugs onto a LaunchPad, which does the commutation; the chip does not spin a motor on its own. Screw terminals for the motor supply (VBAT, PGND) and the three phases (OUT A, B, C); a five-way terminal block for Hall sensors with a jumper that picks their supply (3.3 V, 5 V or external). The PWM mode (6x or 3x), slew rate, current-sense gain and overcurrent level are set by resistors on the board; the program finds the PWM mode at start.
use_for: Spinning a Hall-sensor brushless motor from the LP-AM13E230 (six-step, the bench program)
TI's three-shunt Hall FOC solution on the AM13, once ported from the DRV8323RH BoosterPack
Current-loop and bearing-fault work on a real motor
parts.connect: Plug onto the LaunchPad kit's BoosterPack headers with the screw terminals pointing away from the USB connector: the Hall-block socket (EVM J8) on J2/J4, the nFAULT-side socket (EVM J9) on J1/J3 with its pin 20 (3.3 V) on J1 pin 1. Then its INHA/INLA, INHB/INLB and INHC/INLC are J4 pins 40 to 35 (MCPWM4 1A to 3B on the LP-AM13E230), Hall A, B, C are J4 pins 34, 33, 32 (PB7, PB6, PA12), nSLEEP J1 pin 9 (PA23), nFAULT J1 pin 10 (PA22), DRVOFF J2 pin 13 (PB18), phase-voltage senses J3 pins 26, 25, 24 and bus sense J3 pin 23 (PA17, PA28, PA18, PA16), current senses J3 pins 27 to 29. Motor supply 4.5 to 65 V DC on VBAT and PGND (reverse-polarity protected). Hall supply jumper J13: GVDD (5 V) for most motors. On the LP-AM13E230, switches S6 and S4 must sit at BP so PB6, PB7, PA11 and PA12 reach the headers.

Eight wires: three phases (yellow A, red B, black C) and five Hall lines (red supply 4.5 to 28 V, black ground, blue A, green B, white C; open-collector outputs). Locked-rotor current at full voltage would be 16 A, so the driver's 4.5 A overcurrent limit and the program's duty cap do the protecting.
